v.why: Adding the missing input-to-output identity path gives large gains (runs 11, 15, 17) compared with replacing an existing conv on edge 3.
Without a direct input-output edge, removing edge 5 eliminates one of few remaining paths to the output (runs 2, 7, 10).
When edge 3 is absent, pruning edge 4 removes a critical route to the output node (runs 82, 86, 89).
If node 1 does not feed the output directly, cutting edge 0 removes little information flow (runs 94, 97 vs 93, 100).
Replacing a parameter-free pool on the final edge with a 3x3 conv adds much-needed learnable capacity (runs 71, 78).
Upgrading a pooling first edge to a 3x3 conv gives larger gains than upgrading a conv/skip edge (runs 23, 27).
Swapping an existing learnable 1x1 conv for a 3x3 conv yields smaller gains than filling a skip/pool/none edge (runs 34, 35, 40).
Observed edits to avg_pool on edge 4 were near-neutral when edge 3 was none but consistently harmful otherwise (runs 42, 46, 50).
Removing a convolutional input-output path costs more than removing a skip on edge 3 (runs 64, 67, 70).
Dropping a pooling op on the output edge is cheap or beneficial (run 3), unlike dropping skip or conv there (runs 6, 8).

raw:
Ten hypotheses, chosen from the 100 measurements plus known NAS-Bench-201 structure (an identity 0→3 path matters, and conv-heavy paths beat pool or none):

1. **Edge 3 → skip_connect is better when edge 3 is none.** Runs 11, 15 and 17 gained up to +21 pp. Where edge 3 already held a conv, the edit was mostly neutral to negative.
2. **Edge 5 → none is worse when edge 3 is none.** With no direct input→output path, cutting edge 5 removes one of the few remaining routes to the output (runs 2, 7, 10).
3. **Edge 4 → none is worse when edge 3 is none.** Same reason: the cell loses one of its last output paths (runs 82, 86, 89).
4. **Edge 0 → none hurts less when edge 4 is none.** Node 1 then only feeds edge 2, so removing edge 0 cuts little (runs 94, 97 vs. 93, 100).
5. **Edge 5 → nor_conv_3x3 is better when edge 5 was avg_pool_3x3.** A parameter-free pool on the final edge is replaced with learnable capacity (runs 71, 78).
6. **Edge 0 → nor_conv_3x3 is better when edge 0 was avg_pool_3x3.** Same pool-to-conv upgrade on the first edge (runs 23, 27).
7. **Edge 1 → nor_conv_3x3 is weaker when edge 1 was nor_conv_1x1.** That edge already has a learnable conv, so the gain is smaller (runs 34, 35, 40).
8. **Edge 4 → avg_pool_3x3 hurts less when edge 3 is none.** Results without a skip were near-neutral; most others lost 2–9 pp.
9. **Edge 3 → none is worse when edge 3 was nor_conv_1x1.** Removing a convolutional input→output path lost the most (runs 64, 67, 70).
10. **Edge 5 → none hurts less when edge 5 was avg_pool_3x3.** Dropping a pool on the output edge costs little and even helped in run 3 (+3.8). Removing skip or conv there hurt more.
